applicableAreas: Entire site where proposed structures may be within clearance zones of existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Examined Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan). Both sheets show existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along southern property boundary near street. Sheet 21 shows proposed transformer pad and underground electric lines. However, NO clearance verification exhibits were found. The sheets show facility locations but do NOT include engineered exhibits demonstrating compliance with AEDC § 1.10.3 clearance standards. Neither sheet shows calculated clearance zones, clearance dimensions measured from outer conductors, or exhibits demonstrating that the dual clearance envelope requirements (7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance) are satisfied. No profile or cross-section views with clearance dimensions are provided.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(2) and § 1.10.3 require clearance verification exhibits when proposed structures are located within required clearance zones of existing electric facilities. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes that BOTH clearance envelopes must be satisfied simultaneously and that clearances must be measured from the outer conductor, not pole centerline. Without engineered exhibits demonstrating these calculations, the applicant has not provided evidence of compliance. The burden of proof is on the applicant to demonstrate code compliance through specific exhibits; showing facility locations alone is insufficient.
findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits are not provided, not engineered and sealed, or not included in the permitted plan set. No exhibits demonstrating compliance with both the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors (measured from outer conductor per AEDC § 1.10.3) are visible on the submitted site plan. Please provide engineered and sealed clearance verification exhibits showing both required clearance envelopes around all proposed structures and existing electric facilities.

applicableAreas: All areas where proposed structures may be within clearance zones of existing electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 is a plan-view drawing only. No profile drawings, cross-section drawings, or elevation views showing vertical clearances have been found. While Sheet 21 shows basic building footprints with Finished Floor Elevations (FFE) for each building, no details show building element dimensions such as overhangs, balconies, awnings, or canopies with their heights and horizontal extents relative to existing or proposed electric facilities. No profile views showing clearances between structures and electric facilities/easements are provided.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires profile or cross-section drawings demonstrating clearances when structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) are located within required clearance zones. The grouping regulatory overview explicitly states that 'Profile plans must be engineered, sealed, and drawn to scale showing all building elements (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) with dimensioned clearances.' The applicant has not provided these critical documents, making it impossible to verify clearance compliance in the vertical plane.
findings.comment: Profile or cross-section drawings are not provided demonstrating clearances between proposed structures (including overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies) and existing electric facilities/easements. Please provide engineered profile drawings showing all building elements with dimensions and clearances measured to the outer conductors of overhead electric lines.

applicableAreas: All areas with proposed structures within clearance zones of electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows building footprints with FFE (Finished Floor Elevations) but no detailed dimensions for building elements (overhangs, balconies, awnings). The sheet shows generic labels for 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', and 'Electrical Meters' but these labels lack any dimensional information. No callouts or dimension lines show clearances measured from outer conductors. The existing overhead electric line (OHE) location is noted but with no specific conductor height or clearance calculations. All dimensions and heights necessary for clearance verification from the outer conductor (not pole centerline) are absent.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 requires that clearance dimensions and heights be specified for all building elements where required for clearance verification. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Measure from outer conductor (the actual wire), NOT from pole centerline or pole structure. For three-phase overhead lines, measure from the outermost conductor farthest from the pole. Horizontal clearances are measured as horizontal distance only (not diagonal).' The submitted plans show generic facility locations without the specific dimensional callouts required to verify compliance with these measurement standards. This deficiency prevents verifiable clearance review.
findings.comment: Clearance dimensions and heights are not specified for building elements, or clearances are measured from pole centerline instead of outer conductor. Please provide dimensioned clearance details on profile drawings showing measurement points from the outer conductor of the overhead electric line, with dimensions to all building elements (overhangs, balconies, awnings, canopies).

applicableAreas: Entire site where overhead distribution primary or neutral conductors are present
findings.observation: No clearance verification exhibits of any kind were found on Sheets 9 or 21. The site plan shows an existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along the southern property boundary. However, there are NO exhibits demonstrating either the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance envelope OR the 15-foot radius clearance envelope required by code. Neither envelope is depicted, labeled, or calculated on any submitted sheet.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 establishes two distinct, concurrent clearance requirements: (1) 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and (2) 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes: 'These are separate envelopes with different geometric properties. Both must be met; satisfying one does not satisfy the other. These requirements are in addition to NESC Section 234 baseline requirements, not substitutes for them.' The applicant has provided neither envelope on the submitted plans, failing to demonstrate compliance with this critical dual-requirement standard.
findings.comment: Clearance verification exhibits show only one clearance envelope (or neither envelope) instead of both envelopes required by code. Please provide clearance verification exhibits demonstrating BOTH the 7'-6" horizontal sky-to-ground clearance AND the 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution conductors, clearly showing both envelopes on the same exhibit(s).

applicableAreas: Electric service connection areas; transformer locations
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan). Sheet 21 shows a transformer pad location and underground electric lines with generic labels ('Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Electrical Meters') but no label explicitly identifying 'Point of Service' (POS). Sheet 9 shows 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' but does not label or dimension a specific point of service. The sheet reference to 'Sheet 19 for Profile' was checked; that sheet contains utility tap (water/wastewater) profiles, not electric service information. No explicit service connection point is labeled and dimensioned on the electrical plans or site plan.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(5) requires that the point of service be explicitly shown and labeled on all required plan sheets. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Must identify one point of service and one service voltage (unless exceptions apply). Plans must include one-line diagram of electrical riser.' The applicant has not provided an explicitly labeled point of service with dimensions showing where service enters the site from Austin Energy's infrastructure. This is a fundamental service documentation requirement that must be clearly marked on the plans.
findings.comment: Proposed point of service is not shown and labeled on all required plan sheets. Please clearly label and dimension the point of service on the electrical plan, site plan, and utility plan, specifying the exact location where service is received from Austin Energy.

applicableAreas: Service routing from transformer to buildings
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows underground electric lines routed to transformer pad and to the buildings, marked with generic labels ('Underground Electric Line') and letter 'E' designation on the routing lines. However, the routing is shown as generic blue lines without clear specification of: (1) which line represents primary routing from AE transformer, (2) specific path identification, (3) detailed routing sequence from point of service through transformer to buildings, or (4) conduit specifications. The routing appears generalized rather than specifically engineered to show the primary distribution path from AE's infrastructure.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that primary routing from AE transformer to building be shown on plans. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Must demonstrate approximate location and appropriate space for electric facilities.' While some routing is shown, it lacks the specificity and clarity required for plan review. The generic routing with minimal labeling does not provide sufficient detail to verify that primary distribution from the transformer to each building is clearly documented with proper identification of the primary service path.
findings.comment: Primary routing from AE transformer to building is not clearly shown on plans with adequate specificity and labeling. Please provide detailed routing on the electrical plan showing the specific primary distribution path from the transformer(s) to each building's service entrance with dimensions and specifications.

applicableAreas: Electrical system documentation
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan') contains only a site plan view showing transformer locations, pull boxes, meters, and underground routing. The sheet reference to 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' directs to Sheet 19, which contains utility tap profiles for water and wastewater, not electrical service information. No one-line electrical riser diagram is present on Sheet 21 or referenced on that sheet. No secondary riser configuration showing how power is distributed from the main service entrance to individual building units is shown. The sheet is entirely plan-view without riser details.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electrical plans include: '(1) secondary riser configuration; (2) one-line diagram of electrical riser; (3) plan-view of electrical layout.' The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Must include one-line diagram of electrical riser.' The applicant has provided only the plan-view portion. The critical one-line diagram and secondary riser configuration documentation are completely absent from the submitted plans. These are standard requirements for any new electric service application.
findings.comment: Secondary riser configuration is not shown on plans, or one-line diagram of electrical riser is not provided. Please provide a one-line electrical riser diagram showing the distribution of service from the main service entrance through the secondary system to all buildings and units, drawn to standard electrical schematic conventions.

applicableAreas: All sheets showing electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 shows electric facilities labeled with generic text callouts: 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Electrical Meters', and 'Underground Electric Line'. While these labels ARE legible and visible, they provide NO technical identification of the facilities. Labels do not indicate: (1) type with any specificity, (2) voltage level, (3) capacity/size, (4) ownership (AE vs. Customer), (5) whether underground or overhead, or (6) material specifications. Sheet 9 similarly shows only generic 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)' and 'OHE' labels without detail. The labels fail to provide the level of identification necessary for clear plan review and code compliance verification.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that electric facilities be 'clearly labeled' with identification. The grouping regulatory overview states: 'Generic "existing utility" notation without specifying electric facility type, voltage, size, ownership' is identified as a common violation pattern. The applicant has used generic type-only labels without the required technical specifications. This deficiency prevents Austin Energy and City reviewers from clearly understanding what facilities are shown and their code compliance status.
findings.comment: Electric facilities are not clearly labeled on plans or labels lack facility type identification and technical specifications. Please provide labels for all electric facilities that clearly identify the type (e.g., 'Transformer Pad - AE Owned', 'Service Entrance Conduit', 'Pull Box') along with applicable voltage, size, and ownership information.

applicableAreas: All electric facilities on site and utility plans
findings.observation: Examined all labels on Sheets 21 and 9. Electric facility labels are limited to type descriptions only: 'Electrical Transformer Pad', 'Electrical Pull Box', 'Electrical Meters', 'Underground Electric Line', and 'Transformer Pad (Typ.)', 'OHE'. None of these labels include any of the following required information: (1) size/conduit diameter, (2) conductor gauge, (3) burial depth (for underground facilities), (4) voltage (primary voltage level), (5) ownership designation (AE vs. Customer). Sheet 3 General Notes and Electric Notes do not remedy this deficiency by providing detailed specifications for the electric facilities shown on the design sheets.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires facility labels to include applicable technical specifications. The grouping regulatory overview lists 'Labels missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information' as a common violation pattern. The applicant's generic labels fail this requirement completely. Without this information, reviewers cannot verify code compliance, safety standards, or service adequacy.
findings.comment: Electric facility labels are missing size (conduit diameter, conductor gauge), depth (burial depth for underground), voltage (primary voltage level), or ownership (AE vs. Customer) information. Please revise all facility labels to include applicable technical specifications such as voltage, conduit/conductor size, burial depth, and ownership.

applicableAreas: Legend on general notes sheet
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains a comprehensive legend (Block 6) listing symbols for utilities. Electric facility symbols shown in legend are: (1) Existing Power Pole & Down Guy; (2) Existing Electric Meter; (3) Existing Transformer Pad; (4) Existing Overhead Electric Line; (5) Existing Light Pole. The legend DOES NOT show any symbols for PROPOSED electric facilities. Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows proposed electric facilities including transformer pads, pull boxes, meters, and underground lines, but these use generic text callout labels rather than legend-defined symbols. No legend symbols for proposed transformer pads, proposed pull boxes, proposed meters, or proposed underground lines are provided.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electric facility symbols be 'identified in legend'. The grouping regulatory overview emphasizes: 'Legend symbols that don't match symbols actually used on plans' as a common violation pattern. The applicant has provided a legend with EXISTING facility symbols only, but the plans show PROPOSED facilities without any legend symbols for them. This creates a documentation gap where proposed facilities cannot be clearly identified using the legend. UCM standards require consistent symbol usage across all sheets.
findings.comment: Electric facility symbols are not identified in legend or symbols for proposed electric facilities are missing from the legend. Please provide legend entries for all proposed electric facilities shown on the plans (proposed transformers, proposed pull boxes, proposed meters, proposed underground lines, proposed service connections, and other relevant symbols).

applicableAreas: All sheets showing electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 3 legend shows symbols for EXISTING electric facilities only. Sheet 21 and Sheet 9 show PROPOSED electric facilities using generic text callout labels (e.g., 'Electrical Transformer Pad', rectangles with 'T' labels) that do not correspond to any symbol shown in the Sheet 3 legend. The symbols actually used on Sheet 21 (simple rectangular blocks, circles, and line designations) do not match any symbol table or legend legend. There is no consistency between the legend provided and the symbols/labels actually used to mark proposed facilities throughout the plan set.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Legend symbols do not match symbols actually used in plans'. The grouping regulatory overview identifies this as a common violation: 'Legend symbols that don't match symbols actually used on plans'. The submitted plans fail this requirement. The legend provides symbols for existing facilities only, while the plans use unlabeled/generic representations for proposed facilities. This creates confusion and prevents consistent interpretation of the plans across sheets.
findings.comment: Legend symbols do not match symbols actually used in plans. Please ensure that all symbols used on site plan, utility plan, electrical plan, grading plan, and landscape plan exactly match the symbols shown in the legend, or add legend entries for any symbols used that are not currently in the legend.

applicableAreas: General notes sheet and other sheets
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes) contains the 'Electric Notes' block showing 5 numbered notes addressing Austin Energy requirements (notes 1-5). Immediately below these 5 notes, the same 5 notes are repeated verbatim with no numbering or distinction. The content is identical word-for-word: (1) tree pruning rights, (2) easement provision, (3) tree removal responsibility, (4) clearance maintenance, (5) relocation costs. This exact duplication appears within the same single text block on the same sheet without any functional reason (no differentiation, no variation, no application-specific instances).
findings.reasoning: Reviewer Convention established in the grouping requires that 'Electric notes [should be] consolidated on cover sheet or general notes sheet' (singular instance), not duplicated. The applicant has consolidated the notes to the general notes sheet, which is correct, but then unnecessarily repeated them within the same block, which creates confusion and increases visual clutter without providing additional information. Best practice requires notes to appear once in a consolidated location.
findings.comment: Electric notes are duplicated on the same sheet. Please remove the duplicate electric notes from Sheet 3 and retain only one complete set of consolidated electric notes on the general notes sheet.

applicableAreas: Site plan and utility plan; all property boundaries
findings.observation: Sheets 9 and 21 show utility easements with text labels: '5' P.U.E.', '5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14...', '3' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14...', and others. However, these easements are shown using only text labels and line work similar to other utility lines. They are NOT clearly delineated with visual emphasis (no distinct shading, hatch pattern, bold lines, or graphic distinction) that would make them stand out for clear identification and review. The easements are legible but lack the clear visual delineation that would distinguish them as critical infrastructure protection areas. Facts.md identifies multiple electric easements that must be shown: two 5-foot electric easements, plus 7.5-foot public utility easement, plus others, but their locations and extents are not clearly highlighted.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(i) requires that 'Electric utility easements [be] clearly delineated showing locations and extents on plans'. The grouping guidance states that this is an 'All sites' applicable requirement. Clear delineation means visual distinction that allows reviewers to readily identify and understand easement boundaries. Text labels alone without visual emphasis are insufficient. The applicant must use graphic techniques (color fill, hatch pattern, bold boundary lines, or other standard plan representation) to clearly distinguish easement areas from surrounding site area.
findings.comment: Electric utility easements are not clearly delineated showing locations and extents on plans. Please add clear visual delineation (shading, hatch pattern, or bold boundary lines) to distinguish electric utility easements from the surrounding site area on site plan and utility plan, with labels showing easement width and recorded instrument numbers.

applicableAreas: Electrical plans and service documentation
findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan), Sheet 3 (General Notes), and facts.md project summary. No electrical load information is shown on any sheet. Sheet 21 shows facility locations and routing but no load calculations, service amperage, or projected demand information. Sheet 3 contains Austin Water capacity letters for water and wastewater service showing demands (60 gpm water, 20 gpm wastewater), but no corresponding electrical load letter or documentation from Austin Energy. Facts.md describes the project as 39 townhome units but provides no electrical load requirements. The preliminary electrical design plan contains no load analysis or specification.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(6) requires that 'Projected load [be] required for electric service' for projects with new or upgraded electric service. This project is clearly a new development with 39 units requiring new electric service. The applicant must provide electrical load calculations showing the total demand (in kVA or kW) for the project based on the 39-unit residential load and any common area requirements. This information is required by Austin Energy for service adequacy verification and is fundamental to the preliminary electrical design.
findings.comment: Projected load for electric service is not provided on electrical plans. Please provide the calculated electrical load for the proposed development (in kVA or kW) based on the 39 residential townhome units and any common area electrical requirements, and submit for Austin Energy capacity verification.

applicableAreas: Property boundaries where clearance zones extend across lines
findings.observation: Sheets 9 and 21 show property lines and existing overhead electric line (OHE) labeled along the southern property boundary near Valley View Road. The sheets show that the existing overhead line is located outside the subject property (on the street side). However, without clearance verification exhibits (as noted in deficiency EL-11.1), it is impossible to determine whether required clearance zones extend across the property line boundary. No clearance radius is drawn or calculated on the available sheets. The applicability of this item depends on whether clearances extend beyond property boundaries, which cannot be verified from the submitted evidence.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.10.3 specifies dual clearance zones (7'-6" horizontal and 15-foot radius) that may extend across property boundaries if structures are sufficiently close to the property line. However, without the clearance verification exhibits that should be provided in response to EL-11.1, this specific requirement cannot be evaluated. The determination of whether clearance lines should extend across property boundaries is dependent on the clearance exhibit analysis, which has not been provided.
findings.comment: Cannot verify from available evidence whether required clearance zones from overhead electric facilities extend across property lines. This determination depends on the clearance verification exhibits referenced in deficiency EL-11.1. Please provide clearance verification exhibits that clearly show whether required clearance envelopes extend beyond the subject property boundary.

applicableAreas: Demolition plan for areas with existing utilities
findings.observation: Sheet 8 (Tree Removal & Demolition Plan) guide.md mentions that Block 2 contains 'Notes instructing coordination with the City of Austin for the removal of power poles and electric lines.' However, in the detailed block content provided (Block 9 - Site Demolition Notes), the notes listed (items 1-10) do not include any specific instruction about removing or relocating electric facilities. The demolition notes address tree protection, private utility abandonment, materials removal, and gas/water meter removal, but no electric facility removal is explicitly noted. Block 2 description references power pole and line removal notes, but these are not clearly visible in the transcribed demolition notes content.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1)(ii) requires that 'Existing electric facilities to be removed or relocated [be] clearly labeled on demolition plan'. The grouping guidance states this applies 'Only when existing electric facilities are being removed or relocated.' From facts.md and sheet reviews, the existing site was previously an assisted living facility that was demolished in 2022 (Building Permit 2022-096813 BP - Final). It is unclear from the current plans whether any existing electric infrastructure (poles, lines, transformers) from the prior structure require removal or relocation as part of the current townhome development. If they do, they must be clearly labeled on the demolition plan.
findings.comment: Existing electric facilities to be removed or relocated are not clearly labeled on demolition plan, or the status of existing electric infrastructure from the prior use is unclear. Please clarify on the demolition plan whether any existing electric poles, lines, or transformers from the prior facility remain on site and if so, clearly label them with removal or relocation status.

applicableAreas: Electrical plans and service entrance details
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) is reviewed as the primary electrical design sheet. This sheet shows transformers, pull boxes, meters, and underground routing, but no electrical disconnects are labeled or detailed. The sheet does not show main service disconnects, transformer disconnects, or building-level disconnects. However, the sheet is titled 'Preliminary Electrical Design Plan' and may represent only a preliminary routing plan. Traditional architectural electrical plans (floor plans showing electrical layout, branch circuits, panel locations, and disconnect details) have not been examined, as they do not appear to be included in the 39-sheet site plan submission.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'Disconnects [be] shown and labeled on electrical plans'. This is listed as an 'All sites' requirement. However, the existing site plan submission appears to include only a preliminary electrical site design plan showing routing and facility locations, not detailed architectural electrical plans that would typically show disconnect locations. Without access to complete architectural/electrical plans for the buildings, this requirement cannot be fully verified.
findings.comment: Cannot fully verify from available evidence whether disconnects are shown and labeled on architectural electrical plans, as detailed electrical plans for individual buildings do not appear to be included in this preliminary site plan submission. If architectural electrical plans are required for this project, please provide them showing main service disconnects, transformer disconnects, and building-level disconnects clearly labeled and sized.

applicableAreas: All sheets showing electric facilities
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electric facilities at 1" = 20' scale with clear blue line colors and legible text callouts. Symbols are distinguishable, and overall presentation is clear for the plan-view routing shown. However, on Sheet 9 (Site Plan), electric infrastructure (transformer pad, existing overhead line) is shown with minimal detail and less visual emphasis compared to water, wastewater, and storm drain routing, which are shown with bold lines and extensive callouts. The inconsistency between sheets creates mixed clarity: Sheet 21 is clear, but Sheet 9 provides insufficient electric facility detail relative to other utilities shown.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(1) requires that 'Electric facilities [be] shown clearly and at legible scale on required plans, [with] symbols [that are] not too small to distinguish facility types'. While Sheet 21 meets this standard for the preliminary design plan, Sheet 9 (Site Plan) does not provide equivalent clarity and detail for electric infrastructure. Best practice requires consistent clarity across all sheets showing utilities. The site plan should show electric routing and facilities with comparable prominence to water, wastewater, and storm drain systems.
findings.comment: Electric facilities may not be shown clearly and at legible scale on all required plan sheets. On Sheet 9 (Site Plan), electric facility routing and symbols lack the visual clarity and detail shown for other utilities (water, wastewater, storm drain). Please enhance the electric facility representation on the site plan to provide equivalent clarity, with clearer routing, larger symbols, and more detailed labeling to match the standard used for other utility systems.

applicableAreas: Site layout and electric facility access routes
findings.observation: Sheet 3 (General Notes, Block 8) contains electric notes stating: 'The owner/developer of this subdivision/lot shall provide Austin Energy with any easement and/or access required, in addition to those indicated, for the installation and ongoing maintenance of overhead and underground electric facilities.' This indicates intent to maintain access but does not provide a specific demonstration on the site plan showing that development will NOT limit Austin Energy personnel access. Sheets 9 and 21 show building locations, driveways, and parking areas but do not include marked access routes or explicit documentation that Austin Energy will have clear access to transformer locations, pull boxes, meters, and existing overhead facilities along the property boundary.
findings.reasoning: AEDC § 1.16.0(4) requires that 'Plans [demonstrate] that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities'. While the electric notes express an intention to maintain access, the site plan does not explicitly demonstrate this through marked access routes, width clearances, or traffic pattern design that ensures Austin Energy vehicles can access facilities. This should be shown graphically on the site plan with clear access routes marked to transformers, pull boxes, meters, and easement areas.
findings.comment: Plans do not demonstrate that development will not limit Austin Energy personnel access to current and proposed electric facilities. Please show on the site plan marked access routes or note that access will be maintained to transformer pads, pull boxes, meters, and easement areas, ensuring that service vehicles can reach all electric facilities for maintenance and emergency response.

applicableAreas: CAD file submission
findings.observation: No CAD file information or georeferencing verification has been provided with the site plan submission reviewed. The submission includes PDF/hardcopy plan sheets but no data regarding CAD file technical specifications. UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that electronic AutoCAD files be submitted with specific coordinate system specifications (NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203). Without access to the actual CAD files or documentation of their technical specifications, this requirement cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'CAD files [be] georeferenced with NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 coordinate system as required'. This is an 'All sites' requirement listed in the grouping. However, CAD file compliance cannot be verified from PDF plan sheet review alone. The applicant must submit the CAD files for technical review, or must provide documentation certifying that the files meet these specifications.
findings.comment: Cannot verify from available evidence whether CAD files are georeferenced with NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203. Please provide the AutoCAD CAD files (DWG or DXF format, version 2016 or newer) with certification that they are properly georeferenced to NAD 83 Texas Central Zone 4203 as required by UCM § 1.4.2.6.

applicableAreas: CAD file layers and properties
findings.observation: No CAD file layer information or color property specifications have been provided. The requirement to place electric facilities on specific named layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. MH, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Pole) with magenta color per UCM standards cannot be verified from PDF plan review alone. The PDF sheets show electric facilities in blue color in the plan views, but CAD file layer structure and color properties are not accessible from the PDF format.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 specifies strict CAD layer naming conventions and requires magenta color for electric facilities. This is an 'All sites' requirement. However, CAD file layer and color compliance cannot be verified from PDF submissions. The applicant must submit the actual AutoCAD files or provide a certification documenting that electric facilities are placed on the required layers with proper color coding.
findings.comment: Cannot verify from available evidence whether electric facilities are placed on correct CAD layers (Elec. UG, Elec. OH, Elec. MH, Elec. Transf. OH, Elec. Transf. UG, Elec. Pole) with Magenta color per layer standards. Please provide the AutoCAD files for verification, or submit a certified list documenting the layer names and colors used for all electric facility objects.

applicableAreas: CAD file model space and UCS settings
findings.observation: No CAD file information regarding object placement (model space vs. paper space) or UCS (User Coordinate System) settings has been provided. UCM § 1.4.2.6 requires that 'All required objects [be] in model space with UCS setting to "World"'. This technical specification cannot be verified from PDF plan sheet review and requires access to the actual CAD files.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.4.2.6 specifies that CAD files must have all required objects in model space with UCS set to 'World'. This is an 'All sites' technical requirement for CAD submission. However, this cannot be verified from PDF plan representations. The applicant must submit the AutoCAD files or provide documentation confirming CAD model space and UCS compliance.
findings.comment: Cannot verify from available evidence whether required electric facility objects are in model space or UCS is set to 'World' per UCM § 1.4.2.6 requirements. Please provide the AutoCAD files for technical verification, or submit documentation certifying that all electric facility objects are placed in model space with UCS setting set to 'World'.
